scope: Selected LibreCAD_3 IMAGE boundary queries and path snapping in 3D.
problem: Nearest-point methods previously returned the coordinate origin for every query.
implementation: Project onto each finite boundary segment and select the nearest in 3D; degenerate segments resolve to their endpoint. Entity and path queries share the implementation.
validation: The generated tilted, planar and degenerate nearest-point control failed before the change.

After the change, five focused tests passed, including selected tilted edge and endpoint queries, a vertical degenerate segment, point, planar case, path snap, image bounds and transforms, and selected image persistence.

The default logical-corner snap control failed before the follow-up; after it, six focused tests pass, including corners, entity/path snap IDs and distance filtering. Bounds, nearest queries and corner snaps share one corner calculation.
After the snap follow-up, 71 selected image, builder and layer tests passed.
Headless planar viewer selects a horizontal IMAGE at Z=70, snaps its corner retaining Z, and rejects a distant pick; the selected image and POINT controls pass.

A tilted image edge failed planar picking before the follow-up. The planar query now projects the same finite edges in XY and retains interpolated Z; the headless viewer selects and snaps the tested edge, a distant interior control is rejected, and the original 3D nearest query remains distinct. 85 focused viewer, image, builder and layer tests pass.
limits: Selected horizontal and tilted images pass headless planar-view tests. Other projected geometry, edge-on depth ambiguity, other snap modes and native GUI behavior remain unqualified.
Clipping boundaries, extreme floating-point magnitudes, arbitrary application GUI workflows, and complete image persistence remain unqualified.
